title: ContextMenu
summary: A context menu is a MonarchMenu that opens when the person touches and holds an element, through Modifier.combinedClickable(onLongClick = …). Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For shortcuts to actions on an item in a list or a grid: copy, share, delete. Every action must also be reachable another way, such as a visible More button or the item's own screen.
whenNotToUse: Not as the only way to an action: a long press cannot be seen. Not for actions of a whole screen: use the top app bar's overflow menu.
api: fun Modifier.combinedClickable(interactionSource: MutableInteractionSource? = null, indication: Indication? = null, enabled: Boolean = true, onClickLabel: String? = null, role: Role? = null, onLongClickLabel: String? = null, onLongClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, onDoubleClick: (() -> Unit)? = null, hapticFeedbackEnabled: Boolean = true, onClick: () -> Unit): Modifier

@Composable fun MonarchMenu(expanded: Boolean, onDismissRequest: () -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, offset: DpOffset = DpOffset(MonarchTokens.Space.space0.dp, MonarchTokens.Space.space1.dp), content: @Composable ColumnScope.() -> Unit)

states.name: closed
states.description: A tap opens the item; a long press opens the menu, with haptic feedback.

states.name: open
states.description: The menu is anchored to the item and takes focus; back or a tap outside closes it.

states.name: through TalkBack
states.description: The long-click label and custom actions appear in TalkBack's actions menu.

appearance: The menu is a MonarchMenu in the raised background role with Monarch's medium radius; items use the default text role, and a destructive item the strong danger role. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colors.
platformNotes: The web ContextMenu opens on right-click, Shift F10 or a long press and is composed of Monarch-styled items, checkboxes, radio groups and submenus. On Android a long press opens a MonarchMenu with the same parts as dropdown-menu, anchored to the item rather than at the touch point. A secondary click with a mouse is not a separate event in combinedClickable; a pointer user gets the visible More button. The web's label and modal props have no equivalent. iOS uses contextMenu.
accessibility: onLongClickLabel names the long press, so TalkBack says "double tap and hold to show actions".
Custom accessibility actions expose each menu action directly in TalkBack's actions menu, without opening the menu.
A visible More button opens the same menu, for people who cannot long press and for pointer users.
Items have 48dp touch targets and the menu closes on back.
edgeCases: A long press also starts text selection or drag and drop where those are enabled on the same element; do not combine them.
Place the MonarchMenu in the same Box as the item so it opens next to it.
